title: Appeals and Grievances — Right to the Next Appeal Level
content:
Appeals and Grievances — next appeal level

**Article 1.** Only the appellant's own request moves a Appeals and Grievances case to the tier's next level; it is not escalated on the region's initiative. A case decided upheld, or decided partially overturned (on the part still denied), moves to escalated when the appellant asks for the next level, and the case file is forwarded to it.

**Article 2.** The next level must be asked for no later than the tier's next-level deadline after this tier's decision date. The next-level deadline is counted in calendar days starting the day after the decision date, so the last timely day is the decision date plus the tier's next-level deadline in days and a request on the next day is late. The decision date is the one on the case record.

**Article 3.** The amount in dispute must be at least the tier's next-level minimum, and a hearing after the next level needs at least the tier's hearing minimum.

**Article 4.** A tier whose next level is "none" (Allowable Charge Review, Beneficiary Grievance) is final at the region. The case file is forwarded within the tier's file-forwarding days of the request.

**Article 5.** Each tier applies its own next-level minimum and its own next-level deadline, as set in the tier schedule. Escalation is open exactly when the amount in dispute is at least the tier's next-level minimum and the tier's next-level deadline is greater than zero days.

**Combinations**

| Amount in dispute against the tier's next-level minimum | Tier's next-level deadline | Escalation open |
|---|---|---|
| at or above | greater than zero | yes |
| at or above | zero (no next level) | no |
| below | any | no |

**Hypothetical timing.** A case decided on 2026-04-15 on a tier with a 60-day next-level deadline: the last timely day for the request is 2026-06-14; a request received that day is on time, a request received on 2026-06-15 is late.
